statement: Quaternion multiplication is a non-commutative bilinear arithmetic operation on the four-dimensional real algebra of quaternions. The supplied sources define quaternion multiplication directly rather than deriving it: viewing a quaternion as a pair of complex numbers $(a + bi)1 + (c + di)\mathbf{j} \in \mathbb{C}^2$ with basis $\{1, \mathbf{j}\}$, multiplication is defined by the distributive law subject to the relations $j^2 = -1$, $ij = -ji$, and $k = ij$, producing $a + bi + cj + dk$; equivalently, it is defined via an algebra homomorphism into $M(4, \mathbb{R})$ mapping $1, i, j, k$ to quadruples of $4 \times 4$ matrices such that quaternion multiplication corresponds to matrix multiplication. Because the supplied sources introduce these relations by definition, they contain no derivation of quaternion multiplication.

symbols.meaning: quaternion represented as a + bi + cj + dk or (r, v)

properties.property: Quaternion multiplication is non-commutative in general ($pq \neq qp$).
properties.why: The multiplication of basis elements satisfies anticommutativity $ij = -ji = k$.

properties.property: Two quaternions $p$ and $q$ commute ($pq = qp$) only if they lie in the same complex subplane of $\mathbb{H}$.
properties.why: Every non-real quaternion generates a planar subalgebra isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{H}$ can be viewed as a union of these complex planes intersecting on the real line.

properties.property: Quaternion multiplication is isomorphic to matrix multiplication in $M(4, \mathbb{R})$ across 48 distinct matrix representations.
properties.why: There exist 48 quadruples of $4 \times 4$ matrices (one identity/scalar matrix and three skew-symmetric matrices) that form an algebra homomorphism mapping quaternion products to matrix products.

properties.property: The fourth power of the norm of a quaternion equals the determinant of its $4 \times 4$ matrix representation.
properties.why: Quaternion multiplication is preserved under the matrix homomorphism where quaternion conjugation corresponds to matrix transpose.

properties.property: A quaternion squares to $-1$ if and only if it is a pure vector quaternion with norm 1.
properties.why: Evaluating $q^2 = -1$ for $q = a + bi + cj + dk$ yields $a^2 - b^2 - c^2 - d^2 = -1$ and $2ab = 2ac = 2ad = 0$, which forces $a = 0$ and $b^2 + c^2 + d^2 = 1$.

properties.property: The multiplicative group of nonzero quaternions acts by conjugation $a \mapsto rar^{-1}$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$.
properties.why: Conjugation by any nonzero quaternion $r$ preserves the real scalar part and the norm of the vector part.

assumptions.assumption: Quaternion components $a, b, c, d$ are real numbers.
assumptions.breaks_when: Coefficients are drawn from non-real or non-commutative algebraic structures.

assumptions.assumption: Multiplication satisfies distributivity and the fundamental basis relations $j^2 = -1$, $ij = -ji = k$.
assumptions.breaks_when: Basis relations or distributive multiplication are modified or violated.

failure_modes.signature: Incorrect sign in the vector/imaginary components of the product.
failure_modes.cause: Basis units anticommute ($ij = -ji = k$), making order of multiplication significant.

failure_modes.mode: Assuming $q^2 = -1$ has only two solutions as in $\mathbb{C}$.
failure_modes.signature: Omission of the continuous two-sphere of square roots of $-1$.
failure_modes.cause: Every unit vector quaternion satisfies $q^2 = -1$, yielding an entire 2-sphere of roots.

failure_modes.mode: Attempting conjugation $rar^{-1}$ with a zero quaternion $r = 0$.
failure_modes.signature: Division by zero / undefined multiplicative inverse.
failure_modes.cause: The conjugation action is defined only for elements of the multiplicative group of nonzero quaternions.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so quaternion_multiplication is recorded as a definition
